said: Blood pressure for a first-year nursing student who is new to it

scenes.teach: Blood pressure is the force of blood pushing against the walls of the arteries. It is written as two numbers in millimetres of mercury (mmHg): the systolic pressure over the diastolic pressure, such as 120/80.
says: Every beat of your heart pushes blood into your arteries.
Blood pressure is the force of that blood on the artery walls.
We write it as two numbers, like 120 over 80.
The unit is millimetres of mercury, or mmHg.

scenes.teach: The systolic pressure is the peak pressure when the heart contracts. The diastolic pressure is the lowest pressure, when the heart relaxes between beats.
says: The top number is the systolic pressure.
It is the highest point, when the heart squeezes.
The bottom number is the diastolic pressure, when the heart relaxes.
So which number is higher, and why?
The systolic one, because the heart is pushing hardest.

scenes.teach: A reading at or above 130/80 on repeated checks is often classed as high blood pressure, or hypertension. Nurses record the reading, the arm used and the patient's position.
says: A reading of 130 over 80 or more, again and again, may be hypertension.
That is the word for high blood pressure.
Always write down the reading, the arm you used and how the patient sat.
